competency_fulfillment.rationale: Fourteen of the fifteen samples ask precisely what the competency names. Seed 43 renders 'A rectangle has sides 4 m and 9 m. What is its area in sq m?' keyed at 36, and seed 44 renders 'A square has a side of 7 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' keyed at 49, so side times side and length times width are both computed and the square unit is stated inside the stem.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four cells of shape by unit appear. Squares in metres at seed 500, 'A square has a side of 10 m. What is its area in sq m?'; squares in centimetres at seed 502, 'A square has a side of 42 cm. What is its area in sq cm?'; rectangles in centimetres at seed 605, 'A rectangle has sides 20 cm and 15 cm. What is its area in sq cm?'; and rectangles in metres at seed 606, 'A rectangle has sides 7 m and 8 m. What is its area in sq m?'.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Structure is single step throughout, but seed 601 sets its story in an impossible space: 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 5 cm long and 16 cm wide with square tiles.' A garden five centimetres by sixteen centimetres, covered by 80 tiles, is not a picture a Grade 3 pupil can form, and it undercuts the metre-scale intuition built by items such as seed 46, 'A rectangle has sides 2 m and 11 m. What is its area in sq m?'.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Seeds 45 and 501 are the same item twice, both reading 'A square has a side of 9 m. What is its area in sq m?' with the identical value set 81, 82, 36, 18 merely reordered, and seed 44 differs from seed 50 only by the unit label, 'A square has a side of 7 cm. What is its area in sq cm?' against 'A square has a side of 7 m. What is its area in sq m?'. Apart from the single tiling story at seed 601, every stem in the packet is one of two fixed frames with new numbers dropped in.

competency_alignment.rationale: Seed 601 ends 'How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?' and keys 80, a bare tile count carrying no square unit, whereas this competency asks for an area expressed in sq cm and sq m. That item reads as the neighbouring problem-solving competency; the other fourteen stems name the unit and ask for the area directly, as at seed 604, 'A rectangle has sides 14 cm and 26 cm. What is its area in sq cm?'.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Seed 502, 'A square has a side of 42 cm. What is its area in sq cm?', demands 42 times 42 equal to 1764, and seed 604, 'A rectangle has sides 14 cm and 26 cm. What is its area in sq cm?', demands 14 times 26 equal to 364. Both are two-digit by two-digit multiplication, past the Grade 3 Quarter 1 computational range that the majority of the packet respects, for example seed 606 at 'A rectangle has sides 7 m and 8 m. What is its area in sq m?'.
